files.capacity/scheduler.json: GET /ws/v1/cluster/scheduler (Accept: application/json) — live capacity cluster: root → {default, adhoc, etl → {ingest, transform}}, 3 partitions (default, gpu, ssd), users, health, ACLs
files.capacity/jmx-queuemetrics-root.json: GET /jmx?qry=Hadoop:service=ResourceManager,name=QueueMetrics,q0=root — live (aggregate container counters for the legacy health block)
files.fair/scheduler.json: GET /ws/v1/cluster/scheduler from a real FairScheduler ResourceManager started for capture (rootQueue → {adhoc, etl → {transform}, default})
files.fair/cluster-info.json: GET /ws/v1/cluster/info from the same throwaway FairScheduler RM
files.fifo/scheduler.json: GET /ws/v1/cluster/scheduler from a real FifoScheduler ResourceManager started for capture (0 NodeManagers — the 'empty cluster' shape)
files.fifo/cluster-info.json: GET /ws/v1/cluster/info from the same throwaway FifoScheduler RM

notes: The shared test cluster is Capacity-scheduled and must not be cycled, so the Fair/FIFO payloads come from throwaway ResourceManagers on loopback with disjoint ports (capture script: /tmp/ys-sched-rm/capture_alt_rm.py, run with the cluster's own conf templates). They are genuine Hadoop 3.4.3 Jersey output, just with 0 NodeManagers.
cluster-info.json in this directory is informational; the app reads /api/yarn/info.
